description: Turns the agent into a design agent for the Canvas workspace — author and edit interactive dashboards, pages, data views, and other UI as self-contained mini web apps that match the app's look (dark/light, desktop/mobile). Builds clickable drill-down panels, modals/drawers/popovers, in-place content swaps, live filters and dynamic animated effects — verified by clicking them, and built in rounds (ship the base, then propose features). Includes create, edit, rename, and delete.
skill_summary: USE THIS for any request to build, design, change, or show something visual — a dashboard, page, report, chart, data view, form, mockup, landing page, notes/tool UI, or anything described as a 'design' or 'UI'. It renders a real, live HTML canvas in the Canvas tab (this is how you make a dashboard — NOT the browser, NOT plain chat). Load it and follow its skill the moment a request is about building or editing a visual surface.

levels.minimal: BUILD POSTURE — Minimal: build exactly and only what the user asked for, in one clean round. Do NOT add unrequested panels, charts, or animations, and do NOT push a menu of extra enhancements after — finish the requested canvas, verify it, and stop. Propose more only if the user asks 'what else can you add?'.
levels.rich: BUILD POSTURE — Rich: lean toward a fuller, more interactive result. After shipping and verifying the requested base, proactively propose a short menu (3–5) of concrete, tempting enhancements tailored to THIS canvas (drill-downs, live filters, count-ups, hover popovers) and offer to add them in the next round. Bias toward dynamic, clickable canvases over static ones — but still ship the requested base first and never bloat a single render.

settings.label: Build style
settings.hint: How much the design agent does beyond the literal request. Minimal = build only what's asked, one round, no upsell; Balanced = today's judgment; Rich = ship the base then propose a menu of interactive enhancements to add next. Rides along as a posture note in the agent's prompt — it nudges behaviour, it is not a hard rule.
